name: Technical Feasibility Spike and Architecture Proof
phase: Hypothesis Framing and Assumption Mapping Tactics
hypothesis: We believe that [external API / architecture] can process [X volume] within [Y latency]. We will verify this by deploying an isolated technical spike in a staging environment, and consider it validated if latency remains below 250ms at 1,500 concurrent requests without data loss.

plan.label: Preparation
plan.text: Strip the front end and every non-essential dependency; isolate the one algorithmic or throughput unknown.

plan.label: Execution
plan.text: Build the smallest codebase that can stress the integration, algorithm or pipeline at the target load.

plan.label: Data collection
plan.text: Run automated load scripts and log latency distribution, memory, error codes and compute cost.

planFull.label: Preparation
planFull.text: Strip away all frontend interfaces and non-essential dependencies. Isolate the specific algorithmic or data throughput unknown.

planFull.label: Execution
planFull.text: Build a minimal codebase designed solely to stress-test the core integration, algorithm, or data pipeline.

planFull.label: Data collection
planFull.text: Run automated load scripts, logging latency distributions, memory usage, error codes, and compute costs.

warning.label: Sandbox Isolation Bias
warning.text: A clean staging spike degrades on real edge cases, dirty legacy data and unoptimised production dependencies.

warningFull: A technical architecture that operates smoothly in a clean, isolated staging environment often degrades when exposed to real-world edge cases, dirty legacy data, and unoptimized production dependencies.
